headline: A 2021 House resolution would have censured Representative Maxine Waters over her comments about the Derek Chauvin trial, but the House voted to table it.
what_it_does: This resolution would have formally censured Representative Maxine Waters for comments she made about the trial of Derek Chauvin. It was raised as a question of the privileges of the House, a procedure that lets a member bring a matter about the House's rights or the conduct of a member to the floor. A censure is a formal rebuke by the full House. The House voted on April 20, 2021 to table it or send it back to committee, so it did not go forward.

who_it_affects.how: If adopted, she would have received a formal House censure, which is an official public rebuke, for her comments about the Chauvin trial.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House of Representatives
who_it_affects.how: If adopted, the resolution would have been a formal House disciplinary action against one of its members, and the vote to table it kept that from happening.
